title: The Galois Correspondence for ℂ / ℝ

problemStatement.plain: Prove the Galois correspondence for C/R: intermediate fields correspond bijectively to subgroups of Gal(C/R), which is cyclic of order 2. Since a prime-order group has only two subgroups, there are no intermediate fields other than R and C. This is the Galois-theoretic alternative to the parent entry's tower-law proof.
whyMatters: Answers open question 3 of fundamental-theorem-algebra-oq-04 with a structurally different proof technique.

proven: every intermediate field is bot (R) or top (C)
knownResults.goal: Formalize the Galois correspondence and re-derive no-intermediate-fields from the subgroup lattice.

Establishes IsGalois R C, |Gal(C/R)|=2, cyclic (Z/2Z), the Galois correspondence order-iso, and intermediateField_eq_bot_or_top via Lagrange on the prime-order group.
builtItems: galoisCorrespondence : IntermediateField R C order-iso (Subgroup Gal)op
insights: Normal R C is NOT a default instance; it comes from IsAlgClosure.normal once IsAlgClosure R C is in scope (parent declares it). Algebra.IsSeparable R C IS automatic in char 0.
IsGalois.mk assembles IsGalois from [Algebra.IsSeparable] + [Normal]; IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank returns Nat.card (not Fintype.card).
Counting subgroups of a prime-order group: avoid normality/CommGroup; use Lagrange (Subgroup.card_subgroup_dvd_card) + Nat.dvd_prime + Subgroup.eq_bot_of_card_eq / eq_top_of_card_eq.
The correspondence lands in (Subgroup G)op; OrderDual.ofDual/toDual are defeq, and OrderIso.map_top/map_bot flip top<->bot to recover K=top/bot.
